To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extraction of RNA from archived serum is influenced by the method used and the addition of carrier during extraction is not a good option when assaying miRNAs using sequencing.

(1) miRNAs can be extracted from archived serum samples using multiple RNA isolation methods; (2) addition of nucleic acids based carriers during extraction does not enhance the miRNA yield; (3) the use of carrier molecules during extraction may not be a good choice for miRNA profiling using sequencing.
the choice of the RNA extraction method is crucial for miRNA sequencing and the carrier molecule addition is not recommended for the same.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a pipeline for miRNA profiling using archived serum samples.
identifying the most suitable extraction method to be used for miRNA profiling using archived serum samples and the use of carrier molecules for miRNA extraction.
the development of a pipeline that can be used to study miRNA expression from archived serum samples using next generation sequencing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
it is not possible to draw a conclusion on the best miRNA extraction method.
there is no single extraction method that can be universally recommended.
the extraction method should be optimized for each type of sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a pipeline to extract miRNA from serum samples and we have also identified the most efficient extraction method.
the choice of extraction procedure is important and the addition of a carrier during extraction is not necessary for miRNA sequencing.
we have developed a pipeline for the profiling of miRNA in archived samples using small volume of serum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of extraction method and the addition of nucleic-acid based carriers are critical for obtaining reliable data for downstream miRNA applications.
the use of a carrier molecule in the extraction procedure does not improve the miRNA yield and may even reduce it.
miRNA profiling from archived serum samples can be carried out with small volumes of samples.
